findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The exit code for 'recreate upgrade required' is silently changed from 4 to 3, and 4 is repurposed as FEATURE_DISABLED, breaking any external consumer (CI scripts, operators, existing docs/tests outside this diff) that keyed on exit code 4 meaning 'recreate upgrade required'. A script or tool that previously branched on exit code 4 ('shut down and recreate') will now interpret exit 4 as 'feature disabled' and exit 3 as 'recreate', taking the wrong action during an upgrade; the code comment only documents picocli's own 1/2 codes, not this contract change for downstream consumers.

[ADVISORY] The doc template unconditionally appends --features=rolling-updates to every update-compatibility invocation, so users copying the guide run a preview-flagged command that prints a preview warning on every invocation even when they only wanted the compatibility check, and the flag is baked into docs rather than the server configuration. Users following update-compatibility.adoc pass a preview feature flag as a throwaway CLI argument; when the feature graduates or is renamed, every documented command in this guide silently breaks with the 'not enabled' error, and the flag duplication (template + Dockerfile-custom-image + UpgradeTest) becomes three places to update with no single source of truth.

[BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently changed from 4 to 3 while FEATURE_DISABLED takes over exit code 4, breaking every external consumer that distinguishes results by exit code. Existing scripts/CI/automation that treat exit code 4 as 'recreate upgrade required' now receive 4 only for feature-disabled and 3 for recreate — a recreate-needed deployment is misread as a new, undocumented code (3), and worse, the old 'recreate' signal (4) now means 'feature disabled', so automation takes the wrong remediation action after upgrade. The diff contains no migration note, doc callout, or changelog entry for this contract change.

[BUG] testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error message and never asserts the FEATURE_DISABLED exit code, and no test in the diff asserts the new RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE=3 value. Both exit-code constants added/changed in CompatibilityResult.java (FEATURE_DISABLED=4, RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE=3) are unverified: a regression that returns 0 or swaps the codes passes this suite, reintroducing the exact class of exit-code drift the change was made to fix. testWrongVersions (lines 93-104) asserts error text but not exit code 3 either.

[BUG] The new exit-code row '4' in the documentation table is only reachable via the CLI's new gating, but the doc's exit-code table was not reconciled with the RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE change from 4 to 3. The pre-existing doc rows (m|2, m|3) were authored against the old code where recreate was exit 4; after this diff code emits 3 for recreate while the doc's row-3 entry describes 'deployment must be shut down' without noting the code changed, and operators following the table cannot distinguish whether row 3 refers to the new or old value — the doc and CompatibilityResult.java disagree on which integer maps to recreate.

[ADVISORY] printFeatureDisabled() hardcodes the feature key 'rolling-updates' in the message while the guard in both callers hardcodes Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES, creating three parallel copies of the feature key across AbstractUpdatesCommand, both command run() methods, the docs template (kc.adoc), and Dockerfile-custom-image. When a second gated capability is added to this framework (the stated purpose of a 'compatibility framework'), each copy must be updated independently; the error message and the guard can drift (message names a feature the guard doesn't check). A single Feature param or constant would make the copies unnecessary — deletion test passes.

[ADVISORY] The custom-operator image build now permanently bakes --features=rolling-updates into every custom operator image, including when rolling updates are not used. Operators who build custom images solely for other reasons silently get the preview ROLLING_UPDATES feature enabled in their server image, expanding the blast radius of a preview feature beyond deployments that opted into rolling updates at the CR level; there is no way to opt out of this line's change without editing the Dockerfile.

[ADVISORY] The feature check runs before validateConfig(), so a user who both omitted the required --input option and lacks the feature gets the feature-disabled error, masking the missing-argument diagnostic. Users enabling the feature via a config file misspelling or an operator debugging a compound invocation see only 'feature rolling-updates is not enabled' even when their command line is also invalid, requiring a second run to discover the argument error; validating config first (or reporting both) would surface all problems in one pass.

[BUG] The RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently reassigned from 4 to 3 and 4 is repurposed as FEATURE_DISABLED, breaking any existing automation (CI pipelines, operators, scripts) that branches on exit code 4 meaning 'rolling upgrade not possible, recreate required'. An existing user upgrading without the feature flag previously got exit code 4 = 'recreate upgrade required'; after this change they get exit code 4 = 'feature disabled', and the actual 'recreate' verdict now arrives on code 3, which the comment itself maps to nothing in picocli's exit-code semantics (1=software error, 2=usage error) — scripts that correctly skipped recreate on code 4 before now misread the result, and the change is not traceable to the stated intent of adding a feature flag.

[ADVISORY] The custom operator image build unconditionally enables the preview feature --features=rolling-updates for every consumer of Dockerfile-custom-image, regardless of whether they use rolling updates at all. Every operator user who builds a custom image (the documented path for custom providers/themes) gets a preview, unsupported feature turned on in their server image as a side effect of this PR; they are silently opted into preview-stage behavior with no opt-out in this build path, and preview features carry no compatibility guarantees.

[ADVISORY] testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error message and never asserts the exit code, leaving the newly introduced CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4) exit code with zero test coverage even though the docs table in update-compatibility.adoc promises result '4' as a contract. A regression that returns 0 or 1 instead of 4 when the feature is disabled would pass CI while breaking the documented exit-code contract that automation relies on to distinguish 'feature disabled' from 'recreate required'.

[ADVISORY] The feature gate is duplicated verbatim in three places (UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run, and the hardcoded 'rolling-updates' string repeated in the Dockerfile, docs macro, docs tables, and ENABLE_FEATURE test constant) instead of a single source of truth keyed off Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey(). When the feature graduates from preview (flag removed) or is renamed, six independent hand-maintained sites across four modules must be found and edited in lockstep; missing one yields a command that gate-checks a nonexistent feature or docs that instruct users to pass an invalid flag.

[ADVISORY] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is now 3, which per the adjacent comment is an unmapped value (picocli defines 1=software error, 2=usage error), so the recreate verdict collides with no standard convention and is inconsistently documented as a deliberate non-standard code. Tooling that treats any non-zero, non-2 exit as a command failure cannot distinguish 'recreate upgrade required' (an expected, actionable outcome) from a crash; the next contributor changing exit codes has no contract beyond this one comment to reason against.

[BUG] The diff redefines RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and assigns 4 to a new FEATURE_DISABLED meaning, an unversioned breaking change to the CLI's exit-code contract Existing automation (operators, CI scripts, deployment tooling) that checks exit code 4 to mean 'rolling upgrade not possible, recreate required' now receives 3 for that condition; worse, a caller that still maps 4 to 'recreate' will interpret the new FEATURE_DISABLED exit as 'perform a recreate upgrade' and take a destructive downtime action when the actual problem is only a missing preview flag

[ADVISORY] The feature-gate guard (Profile.isFeatureEnabled check + printFeatureDisabled + picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED)) is duplicated verbatim in UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata, and the disabled-feature message hardcodes the literal 'rolling-updates' inside AbstractUpdatesCommand When a second gated command or a second gated feature is added, one of the copies will drift (wrong exit code or wrong feature name in the message); extracting the guard into AbstractUpdatesCommand parameterized by the feature would leave one place to update

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff asserts the numeric exit codes: testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error message, and no test asserts the new RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE value of 3 A regression that flips FEATURE_DISABLED and RECREATE_UPGRADE constants (or reverts 3 back to 4) passes this suite green while breaking the external exit-code contract that scripts depend on

[ADVISORY] The comment 'see picocli.CommandLine.ExitCode' is misleading: picocli defines 0/1/2, and the value 3 chosen here matches neither picocli's software error (1) nor usage error (2), so the comment implies an authority the constant does not have The next editor reads the comment and assumes 3 is a picocli-reserved/meaningful code; the comment should state these are Keycloak-own contract codes distinct from picocli's, or the mismatch silently documents the wrong provenance

[BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was silently changed from 4 to 3 and the value 4 was repurposed as FEATURE_DISABLED, with no documented contract change or explicit acceptance of the exit-code semantic shift. Any existing automation (CI pipelines, operator scripts, ad-hoc scripts) that interprets exit code 4 as 'recreate upgrade required' will now interpret FEATURE_DISABLED (4) as a recreate verdict and take a deployment down for a recreate when the actual condition is merely a disabled preview feature — the exact destructive-downtime action the compatibility tool exists to prevent; conversely, scripts expecting 4 for recreate now see 3 and can no longer distinguish recreate from a generic software error (picocli exit 1) except by raw integer.

[ADVISORY] printFeatureDisabled hardcodes the feature name 'rolling-updates' into a shared AbstractUpdatesCommand helper, even though the check is duplicated inline in two subclasses rather than parameterized. When a second update command or a differently-gated command reuses this helper, the message will name the wrong feature; the next maintainer adding a gate must also edit the message string, and the current two copies of the identical guard block (UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java:46-50, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java:46-50) will drift.

[ADVISORY] The updatecompatibility doc macro now hardcodes --features=rolling-updates into every generated command example, coupling all downstream documentation to the preview flag permanently. When the feature is promoted to default-enabled (or renamed), every guide page using this macro silently instructs users to pass a flag that no longer exists or is unnecessary; the single macro was chosen to avoid duplication but now embeds a preview-stage detail into a stable template, so removal later requires hunting call sites rather than flipping the feature's Type.

[ADVISORY] testMissingOptionOnSave was retargeted to run with the feature enabled but still asserts assertNoMessage("Missing required argument"), asserting the absence of the very error the scenario should produce. The test now passes vacuously regardless of whether the save command validates its required option: if the missing-argument validation regresses or is deleted, no assertion fails, so the diff's own test suite cannot detect loss of the contract it claims to cover.

[ADVISORY] The diff changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 (CompatibilityResult.java line 31-34), a documented external contract, but no test in the diff asserts any non-zero exit code, so the new 3 (and the collision risk with picocli's USAGE exit code 2) is never verified. External consumers (operator scripts, CI tooling) that branch on the exit code get a silently changed value (3 instead of 4) with zero test coverage; a future regression back to a wrong constant would pass the suite, since testWrongVersions asserts only error message text and never result.exitCode().

[ADVISORY] testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error message text and never asserts the FEATURE_DISABLED exit code (4), which is the machine-consumable part of the new behavior and the value documented in the update-compatibility.adoc exit-code table added in this same diff. If picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) is dropped or the constant drifts, callers scripting around the documented 'exit code 4 = feature disabled' contract break while the test suite stays green, since a passing CLI run (exit 0) also satisfies cliResult.assertError(...) assertions in this harness.

[BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is repurposed from 4 to 3 in the same PR that introduces FEATURE_DISABLED=4, so every existing consumer of the check command's exit codes sees its meaning silently changed. Automation (CI pipelines, operator scripts, upgrade tooling) that checks exit code 4 to decide 'recreate required' will now receive 3 for that outcome and 4 for 'feature disabled'; old consumers interpret a feature-disabled run as 'recreate required' and a recreate outcome as an unknown/generic error, silently redirecting upgrade decisions — this is a breaking contract change shipped without a version gate or expand/contract step.

[ADVISORY] The shared documentation template hardcodes '--features=rolling-updates' into the update-compatibility command for every page that includes the macro, coupling all documented invocations to the preview flag name. When the feature graduates from preview (flag removed or renamed, or made default-enabled), every doc page silently documents a command that fails with 'Unknown option' or an unnecessary flag; operators copy-pasting from docs get a failing command, and each of the per-guide call sites must be hunted down and edited individually because the flag is baked into the shared template rather than passed as a parameter.

[ADVISORY] The custom-image Dockerfile unconditionally bakes '--features=rolling-updates' into the build step, so every image built from this recipe permanently enables a preview feature. Users of the custom-image recipe get preview rolling-updates behavior (and its preview-stage operator failure mode when the feature is later removed/renamed) without opting in; since the flag is frozen into the image build, changing it requires rebuilding the image rather than a config change.

[ADVISORY] FEATURE_DISABLED is assigned exit code 4, the exact value RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE had before this change, so existing automation branching on '4 means recreate upgrade required' now silently misreads a feature-disabled failure as a recreate verdict. Scripts, operators, or CI jobs written against the previous contract (documented in update-compatibility.adoc's table where result 4 previously did not exist but 4 was the recreate code in code) treat a disabled-feature run as 'deployment must be shut down / recreate required', taking the wrong remediation path with no error indicating the real cause; the new docs table only renumbers the human-facing meaning, not the code-level contract consumers compiled against.

[ADVISORY] The feature-disabled guard exits with picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED) before validateConfig(), so a run that is both missing the required --input option and missing the feature flag reports only the feature error and masks the usage error the user would otherwise see. A user following older docs (which omit --features) gets a single misleading 'feature not enabled' message even when their command is also malformed, requiring a second round-trip to discover the missing-argument error; minor diagnostic friction, not data loss.

[ADVISORY] The preview feature flag is baked into the image build (--features=rolling-updates) rather than passed at run time, coupling the custom-image recipe to a preview feature that is scheduled to change or be removed. When the feature is promoted to default or removed, every operator deployment built from this Dockerfile carries a stale build-time flag that either becomes dead config or fails build validation on the next release, silently breaking the custom-image upgrade path that this diff's own tests rely on.
